relevance_note: Case report of one ABCA1 compound heterozygote: "Whole-exome sequencing of the patient identified two compound heterozygous mutations in the ABCA1 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper; rows written by a short Python script from my own reading (no table transcription). Scope: the index patient plus three previously published patients summarized in the Discussion with individual-level facts (Negi et al. [19], Hovingh et al. [20], Per et al. [16]). For [19] and [20] the text does not name the diagnosis for each person; inclusion rests on the paragraph context (Tangier disease case reports), so disease_label is 'not reported' for them. Ref [16] patient's sex is left 'not reported' (only the reference-list title says 'adolescent girl'). The sentence 'the elevated threshold for proprioceptive sensitivity, as revealed by QST' in the Per et al. paragraph is ambiguous (it is repeated for 'our patient' in the next paragraph), so it is attributed only to the index patient. 'In these cases, the presence of pain was not mentioned' / 'the report does not describe the presence of pain' are silence, not exclusions. Variants are printed in allele bracket notation 'NM_005502.4:c.[16C>T];[5520del]' and 'NP_005493.2:p.[(Gln6Ter)];[(p.Phe1840LeufsTer30)]'; I split them into two rows, keeping each bracket as printed ('c.[16C>T]', '[5520del]'; 'p.[(Gln6Ter)]', '[(p.Phe1840LeufsTer30)]') without rewriting them; the c. prefix and transcript NM_005502.4 are shared by both. Protein reference NP_005493.2 is printed but has no field. Pathogenicity left 'not reported': the paper says the variants were 'classified as pathogenic in the ClinVar database', which is a database classification, not the authors' own. Inheritance and parental testing left 'not reported': the paper says only 'The segregation of the variants was confirmed by Sanger DNA sequencing in available family members', without naming parents or results per relative; no relatives are described, so none get rows. Variant type not stated by the authors. Functional tests (Timed Up and Go, Box and Block, Five Times Sit to Stand, Unipedal Stance, Six-Minute Walk 564 m vs normal 576-700 m) and per-limb QST percentiles in Table 1 were not recorded as features; the paper does not label them normal or abnormal individually. 'She had a normal gait' recorded as excluded 'gait disturbance' (D-27). Checklist 'reduced deep sensation' marked observed from hyposensitivity to vibratory stimuli; splenomegaly and hepatomegaly marked observed from 'palpable hepatosplenomegaly'; for ref [19] 'peripheral neuropathy' marked observed from a prior diagnosis of 'pressure neuropathy of the median and ulnar nerves'. No contradictions found in the paper.
